subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: What permanent multi-index memory failover contract should OpenClaw support before implementation begins?
rationale: The request crosses public config, stored SQLite/index layout, provider routing, status surfaces, and migration policy, so automation cannot safely choose the durable API or rollout semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a multi-index design
options.body: Define the supported indexes/activeIndex/fallbackIndexes contract, migration story, and observability requirements before any implementation PR.

options.title: Limit near-term work to recovery bugs
options.body: Keep current single-index semantics and handle only narrower failures such as the fallback-latch recovery issue.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave the shipped identity guard and manual reindex workflow as the supported behavior until memory architecture priorities change.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a multi-index design
recommendation.body: Define the supported indexes/activeIndex/fallbackIndexes contract, migration story, and observability requirements before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is assigned on the live issue and has adjacent memory index identity/fallback history, making them the best available decision owner from the evidence.
